claim: Beige adipocytes in mouse inguinal subcutaneous white fat (iWAT) associate with dense sympathetic neurites.
source: While beige adipocytes have been found to associate with dense sympathetic neurites in mouse inguinal subcutaneous white fat (iWAT), little is known about when and how this patterning is established.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established finding that motivates the current study.

claim: Parenchymal neurites actively grow in iWAT between postnatal day 6 (P6) and P28.
source: We found that parenchymal neurites actively grow between postnatal day 6 (P6) and P28, overlapping with early postnatal beige adipogenesis.
evidence: This finding is based on whole-tissue imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Early postnatal beige adipogenesis overlaps temporally with parenchymal neurite growth.
source: We found that parenchymal neurites actively grow between postnatal day 6 (P6) and P28, overlapping with early postnatal beige adipogenesis.
evidence: This temporal overlap is demonstrated through imaging and gene expression data.

claim: Constitutive deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes reduces early postnatal beige adipocytes.
source: Constitutive deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes led to a significant reduction in early postnatal beige adipocytes and sympathetic density within this window.
evidence: This is supported by imaging and gene expression data from constitutive Prdm16 knockout mice.

claim: Constitutive deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes reduces sympathetic density in iWAT during early postnatal development.
source: Constitutive deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes led to a significant reduction in early postnatal beige adipocytes and sympathetic density within this window.
evidence: This is demonstrated through whole-tissue imaging and quantification of sympathetic innervation.

claim: Prdm16 is required for guiding sympathetic growth during early development.
source: Using an inducible, adipocyte-specific Prdm16 knockout model, we found that Prdm16 is required for guiding sympathetic growth during early development.
evidence: This is based on experiments using inducible Prdm16 deletion during the perinatal period.

claim: Deleting Prdm16 in adult animals does not affect sympathetic structure in iWAT.
source: Deleting Prdm16 in adult animals, however, did not affect sympathetic structure in iWAT.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments with adult-specific Prdm16 deletion.

claim: Beige adipocyte-sympathetic neurite communication is crucial to establish sympathetic structure during the early postnatal period.
source: Together, these findings highlight that beige adipocyte-sympathetic neurite communication is crucial to establish sympathetic structure during the early postnatal period but may be dispensable for its maintenance in mature animals.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined results of developmental timing studies and Prdm16 deletion experiments.

claim: Beige adipocyte-sympathetic neurite communication may be dispensable for maintenance of sympathetic structure in mature animals.
source: Together, these findings highlight that beige adipocyte-sympathetic neurite communication is crucial to establish sympathetic structure during the early postnatal period but may be dispensable for its maintenance in mature animals.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect of adult Prdm16 deletion on sympathetic structure.

claim: White adipose tissue enables safe storage and rapid mobilization of energy in response to nutritional needs.
source: White adipose tissue enables the safe storage and rapid mobilization of energy in response to nutritional needs, while brown adipose tissue defends body temperature by dissipating energy as heat (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from established literature (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).

claim: Brown adipose tissue defends body temperature by dissipating energy as heat.
source: White adipose tissue enables the safe storage and rapid mobilization of energy in response to nutritional needs, while brown adipose tissue defends body temperature by dissipating energy as heat (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from established literature (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).

claim: Excess high-calorie foods, sedentary lifestyle, and thermal comfort have contributed to overexpansion of white fat.
source: In modern times, however, excess high-calorie foods, a sedentary lifestyle, and thermal comfort have contributed to an overexpansion of white fat and a relative paucity of brown fat (Heymsfield and Wadden, 2017; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from literature (Heymsfield and Wadden, 2017; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2018).

claim: Modern lifestyle factors have contributed to a relative paucity of brown fat.
source: In modern times, however, excess high-calorie foods, a sedentary lifestyle, and thermal comfort have contributed to an overexpansion of white fat and a relative paucity of brown fat (Heymsfield and Wadden, 2017; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from literature (Heymsfield and Wadden, 2017; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2018).

claim: Obesity affects over 40% of adults in the United States.
source: Obesity now affects over 40% of adults in the United States and over 600 million adults worldwide (CDC, 2020a; The GBD 2015 Obesity Collaborators, 2017).
evidence: This statistic is cited from CDC, 2020a.

claim: Obesity affects over 600 million adults worldwide.
source: Obesity now affects over 40% of adults in the United States and over 600 million adults worldwide (CDC, 2020a; The GBD 2015 Obesity Collaborators, 2017).
evidence: This statistic is cited from The GBD 2015 Obesity Collaborators, 2017.

claim: Obesity-related medical care costs the United States health care system nearly $150 billion each year.
source: Excess adiposity is at the center of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality, and obesity-related medical care costs the United States health care system nearly $150 billion each year (CDC, 2020b).
evidence: This cost estimate is cited from CDC, 2020b.

claim: Thermogenic brown and beige adipocytes convert lipids and glucose into heat, thereby increasing energy expenditure.
source: While white adipocytes store excess energy, thermogenic brown and beige adipocytes convert lipids and glucose into heat, thereby increasing energy expenditure (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from established literature (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).

claim: Murine beige adipocytes resemble human brown adipocytes in their molecular signature.
source: Unlike classical brown adipocytes which are thermogenic in basal conditions, murine beige adipocytes, which resemble human brown adipocytes in their molecular signature (Shinoda et al., 2015), reside in white adipose depots and need to be activated by external stimuli such as the sympathetic nervous system to drive thermogenesis (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014; Wang and Seale, 2016).
evidence: This is cited from Shinoda et al., 2015.

claim: Beige adipocytes reside in white adipose depots and need to be activated by external stimuli to drive thermogenesis.
source: Unlike classical brown adipocytes which are thermogenic in basal conditions, murine beige adipocytes, which resemble human brown adipocytes in their molecular signature (Shinoda et al., 2015), reside in white adipose depots and need to be activated by external stimuli such as the sympathetic nervous system to drive thermogenesis (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014; Wang and Seale, 2016).
evidence: This is cited from literature (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014; Wang and Seale, 2016).

claim: Activation of thermogenic adipocytes in rodents and humans is associated with increased whole-body energy expenditure.
source: Recent studies have shown that activation of thermogenic adipocytes in both rodents and humans is associated with increased whole-body energy expenditure, improved glucose homeostasis, and enhanced insulin sensitivity (Becher et al., 2021; Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014; Seale et al., 2011; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009), suggesting a new approach to defend against obesity.
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Becher et al., 2021; Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014; Seale et al., 2011; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009).

claim: Activation of thermogenic adipocytes is associated with improved glucose homeostasis.
source: Recent studies have shown that activation of thermogenic adipocytes in both rodents and humans is associated with increased whole-body energy expenditure, improved glucose homeostasis, and enhanced insulin sensitivity (Becher et al., 2021; Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014; Seale et al., 2011; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009), suggesting a new approach to defend against obesity.
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Becher et al., 2021; Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014; Seale et al., 2011; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009).

claim: Activation of thermogenic adipocytes is associated with enhanced insulin sensitivity.
source: Recent studies have shown that activation of thermogenic adipocytes in both rodents and humans is associated with increased whole-body energy expenditure, improved glucose homeostasis, and enhanced insulin sensitivity (Becher et al., 2021; Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014; Seale et al., 2011; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009), suggesting a new approach to defend against obesity.
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Becher et al., 2021; Cypess et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014; Seale et al., 2011; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009).

claim: Both brown and beige adipocytes are surrounded by dense sympathetic neurites termed parenchymal innervation.
source: Although located in distinct fat depots, both brown and beige adipocytes are surrounded by dense sympathetic neurites, termed parenchymal innervation (Blaszkiewicz et al., 2019; Chi et al., 2018b; Guilherme et al., 2019; Jiang et al., 2017; Wirsen, 1964).
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Blaszkiewicz et al., 2019; Chi et al., 2018b; Guilherme et al., 2019; Jiang et al., 2017; Wirsen, 1964).

claim: Norepinephrine released by parenchymal neurites activates β-adrenergic signaling in thermogenic adipocytes.
source: Norepinephrine, a neurotransmitter released by these parenchymal neurites, activates β-adrenergic signaling in thermogenic adipocytes, resulting in enhanced thermogenesis and lipolysis (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004; Hsieh and Carlson, 1957).
evidence: This is cited from literature (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004; Hsieh and Carlson, 1957).

claim: β-adrenergic signaling in thermogenic adipocytes results in enhanced thermogenesis and lipolysis.
source: Norepinephrine, a neurotransmitter released by these parenchymal neurites, activates β-adrenergic signaling in thermogenic adipocytes, resulting in enhanced thermogenesis and lipolysis (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004; Hsieh and Carlson, 1957).
evidence: This is cited from literature (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004; Hsieh and Carlson, 1957).

claim: S100B in brown adipocytes is an important molecular determinant of sympathetic innervation in brown fat.
source: Recent studies have identified S100B and TGFβ1 in brown adipocytes as important molecular determinants of sympathetic innervation in brown fat (Hu et al., 2020; Zeng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from recent studies (Hu et al., 2020; Zeng et al., 2019).

claim: TGFβ1 in brown adipocytes is an important molecular determinant of sympathetic innervation in brown fat.
source: Recent studies have identified S100B and TGFβ1 in brown adipocytes as important molecular determinants of sympathetic innervation in brown fat (Hu et al., 2020; Zeng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from recent studies (Hu et al., 2020; Zeng et al., 2019).

claim: The density of sympathetic parenchymal neurites in close apposition to beige adipocytes is dependent on PRDM16.
source: Assisted by a whole-adipose immunolabeling and clearing method, called Adipo-Clear, we recently found that the density of sympathetic parenchymal neurites in close apposition to beige adipocytes is dependent on PRDM16 (PR domain containing 16), the transcriptional determinant of beige adipocyte identity and function (Chi et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is cited from the authors' previous work (Chi et al., 2018b).

claim: PRDM16 is the transcriptional determinant of beige adipocyte identity and function.
source: Assisted by a whole-adipose immunolabeling and clearing method, called Adipo-Clear, we recently found that the density of sympathetic parenchymal neurites in close apposition to beige adipocytes is dependent on PRDM16 (PR domain containing 16), the transcriptional determinant of beige adipocyte identity and function (Chi et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is cited from the authors' previous work (Chi et al., 2018b).

claim: Deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes led to ablation of beige adipocyte function and dramatically reduced parenchymal innervation density.
source: Specifically, deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes led to ablation of beige adipocyte function and dramatically reduced parenchymal innervation density, suggesting that beige adipocyte-associated factors regulate the structure of sympathetic innervation.
evidence: This is cited from the authors' previous work (Chi et al., 2018b).

claim: At P2, adipocytes in iWAT appeared fully vascularized and organized into distinct lobular structures.
source: At this stage, adipocytes appeared fully vascularized and organized into distinct lobular structures, as shown by the endothelial cell marker PECAM (also known as CD31) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,C and F), consistent with previous reports (Hong et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,C and F) and cited from Hong et al., 2015.

claim: Dense parenchymal innervation in close apposition to adipocytes was not obvious at P2.
source: While we could detect TH-positive (TH+) signals resembling nerve fascicles as well as fibers wrapping around large blood vessels, dense parenchymal innervation in close apposition to adipocytes, which was reported in adult iWAT (Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017), was not obvious at this age (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–F).

claim: At P6, sympathetic fibers in iWAT travel in parallel within nerve fascicles.
source: At P6, more distinct features of sympathetic innervation in iWAT were observed: (a) travelling in parallel within nerve fascicles and (b) wrapping around main blood vessels in a dense mesh-like morphology (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).

claim: At P6, sympathetic fibers in iWAT wrap around main blood vessels in a dense mesh-like morphology.
source: At P6, more distinct features of sympathetic innervation in iWAT were observed: (a) travelling in parallel within nerve fascicles and (b) wrapping around main blood vessels in a dense mesh-like morphology (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).

claim: Sympathetic fibers leave the nerve fascicle and wrap around the main blood vessel as the first order of innervation.
source: Specifically, we found several convergence points where TH+ nerve fibers within a nerve fascicle deviated from the bundle and merged with the innervation of the central blood vessel (Figure 1B–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C, Figure 1—video 1), suggesting that sympathetic fibers leave the nerve fascicle and wrap around the main blood vessel as the first order of innervation.
evidence: This is inferred from imaging data (Figure 1B–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C, Figure 1—video 1).

claim: The main blood vessel innervation extends around branching arterioles and venules as the second order of innervation.
source: Subsequently, the main blood vessel innervation extended around branching arterioles and venules as the second order of innervation (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F, Figure 1—video 1).

claim: The majority of nerve fibers follow capillaries to arrive in the tissue parenchyma.
source: Lastly, discrete nerve fibers became apparent at the terminals of the second-order innervation to project into tissue parenchyma, where adipocytes are located. Notably, the majority of these nerve fibers appeared to follow capillaries to arrive in the tissue parenchyma (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2G–J).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2G–J).

claim: Sympathetic axons in iWAT first grow along the vasculature before reaching the tissue parenchyma.
source: The results from P2 and P6 samples indicate that the sympathetic axons in iWAT first grow along the vasculature before reaching the tissue parenchyma, consistent with previous findings showing that developing sympathetic axons follow the vasculature to reach their target organs (Glebova and Ginty, 2005).
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data and cited from Glebova and Ginty, 2005.

claim: Dense parenchymal innervation surrounding adipocytes is not established at P6.
source: However, dense parenchymal innervation surrounding adipocytes, which several studies have characterized in mature iWAT (Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017), is not established at P6.
evidence: This is based on imaging data and cited from Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017.

claim: Dense parenchymal neurites surrounding adipocytes first became apparent at P10 in the inguinal region.
source: Remarkably, adipocyte-innervating neurites became apparent four days later. In the inguinal region, dense parenchymal neurites surrounding adipocytes were first found at P10, in particular within lobules at the core of this region (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K, Figure 1—figure supplement 3D, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K, Figure 1—figure supplement 3D, Figure 1—video 2).

claim: At P14, the number of lobules containing dense parenchymal neurites dramatically increased in the inguinal region.
source: At P14, the number of lobules that contain dense parenchymal neurites dramatically increased, spreading outwards from the core of the inguinal region (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 3F, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 3F, Figure 1—video 2).

claim: The emergence of dense parenchymal neurites in the dorsomedial region lagged behind the inguinal region.
source: Interestingly, the emergence of dense parenchymal neurites in the dorsomedial region lagged behind. While parenchymal neurites were detectable in the dorsomedial region at P14 and P21 (Figure 1H–I, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E & G, Figure 1—video 2), we did not observe densely innervated lobules that resemble the adult innervation pattern in this region until P28 (Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 3I, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1H–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E,G,I, Figure 1—video 2).

claim: The dorsolateral region of iWAT remained sparsely innervated relative to other regions throughout the early postnatal period.
source: Notably, the dorsolateral region of iWAT remained sparsely innervated relative to the inguinal region and the dorsomedial region throughout the early postnatal period (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,C,E,G & I, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,C,E,G,I, Figure 1—video 2).

claim: Beige adipocytes first emerge in iWAT at P6 in the core of the inguinal region.
source: Specifically, we found that beige adipocytes first emerge in iWAT of P6 animals that were born and housed at room temperature, as shown by a few UCP1+ adipocytes sparsely distributed in the core of the inguinal region, close to the inguinal lymph node (Figure 2A–B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2A–B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).

claim: At P10, clusters of UCP1+ adipocytes were located in distinct lobules in the core of the inguinal region.
source: At P10, we detected clusters of UCP1+ adipocytes located in distinct lobules in the core of the inguinal region (Figure 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).

claim: At P14, lobules containing UCP1+ adipocytes expanded from the core of the inguinal region.
source: Four days later, at P14, the lobules containing UCP1+ adipocytes further expanded from the core (Figure 2E & G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2E,G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).

claim: At P21 and P28, extensive UCP1+ lobules occupied a significant portion of the inguinal region.
source: At P21 and P28, extensive UCP1+ lobules occupied a significant portion of the inguinal region, comparable to the extent of UCP1+ cells only seen in adult animals after cold exposure (Figure 2H and J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C,G, & H).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2H,J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C,G,H).

claim: UCP1+ adipocytes in the dorsomedial region first emerged in small clusters at P14.
source: On the other hand, the emergence of UCP1+ adipocytes in the dorsolumbar region again lagged behind. UCP1+ adipocytes in the dorsomedial region first emerged in small clusters at P14 and then as distinct lobules at P21 (Figure 2E–F & and H–I).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2E–F,H–I).

claim: The dorsolateral region was devoid of UCP1+ adipocytes at all stages analyzed during early postnatal development.
source: Interestingly, the dorsolateral region was devoid of UCP1+ adipocytes at all stages analyzed (Figure 2A,C,E and H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A & D–H).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2A,C,E,H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D–H).

claim: Ucp1 mRNA expression showed a gradual increase from P6 to P14 in the inguinal region.
source: In line with the imaging results, Ucp1 mRNA expression showed a gradual increase from P6 to P14 in the inguinal region (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).

claim: Ucp1 mRNA levels peaked around P12-P16 in the inguinal region.
source: To our surprise, although we observed more extensive UCP1+ adipocytes in the inguinal region at P21 and P28 by imaging, Ucp1 mRNA levels peaked around P12-P16, with the expression level at P14 being fourfold and eightfold higher than that of P21 and P28, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).

claim: Beige adipocytes arising in the inguinal region during early postnatal development may exhibit peak thermogenic potential around 2–3 weeks of age.
source: These quantitative transcriptional data suggest that the beige adipocytes arising in the inguinal region of iWAT during early postnatal development may exhibit peak thermogenic potential around 2–3 weeks of age and gradually become less active as animals mature.
evidence: This is inferred from the qPCR data showing peak Ucp1 expression at P14.

claim: Prdm16 showed a consistent 1.5- to twofold increase in mRNA levels in the inguinal relative to the dorsolumbar region across all time points.
source: Of note, Prdm16, the transcriptional coregulator that determines beige adipocyte phenotype, showed a consistent 1.5- to twofold increase in mRNA levels in the inguinal relative to the dorsolumbar region across all time points (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).

claim: There is a dramatic overlap between the presence of dense parenchymal innervation and beige adipocytes from P10 onwards.
source: When we overlaid the UCP1 and TH signals, we observed a dramatic overlap between the presence of dense parenchymal innervation and beige adipocytes, particularly from P10 onwards (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–J, Figure 1—video 2), strongly suggesting that early postnatal beige adipocytes are associated with the signals enabling sympathetic axon growth.
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–J, Figure 1—video 2).

claim: Early postnatal beige adipocytes and sympathetic neurites arise in iWAT with the same patterning when mice are raised at 30°C as at room temperature.
source: When mice were born and raised at a warmer temperature (30°C), at which cold-induced sympathetic firing is minimized, early postnatal beige adipocytes and sympathetic neurites arise in iWAT with the same patterning as that of room temperature-housed mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3K–L).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3K–L).

claim: The development of beige adipocytes is likely not dependent on sympathetic activation.
source: In addition, a recent study using genetic sympathetic ablation showed that early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in the absence of sympathetic innervation (Wu et al., 2020b). Together, these data suggest that the development of beige adipocytes is likely not dependent on sympathetic activation, but rather based on a developmentally hard-wired program.
evidence: This is inferred from the thermoneutrality data and cited from Wu et al., 2020b.

claim: At P6, the sympathetic nervous system develops similarly in both control and cPrdm16KO mice.
source: At P6, we observed minimal beige adipocytes and scant parenchymal innervation in both control and cPrdm16KO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–H), suggesting that the sympathetic nervous system develops similarly in both models prior to the emergence of beige adipocyte clusters.
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–H).

claim: At P14, deletion of Prdm16 completely ablated beige adipocytes in the inguinal region at both mRNA and protein levels.
source: At P14, the deletion of Prdm16 completely ablated beige adipocytes that normally arise in the inguinal region of control mice, both at the mRNA and protein levels (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is based on qPCR and imaging data (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).

claim: At P14, the increase in parenchymal innervation density in the inguinal region of control mice was not observed in cPrdm16KO mice.
source: Correspondingly, the increase seen in parenchymal innervation density in the inguinal region of control mice was not observed in cPrdm16KO mice (Figure 3A–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 3A–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).

claim: At P21, cPrdm16KO mice showed ablation of beige adipocytes and lack of growth in parenchymal innervation.
source: At P21, we observed similar ablation of beige adipocytes and lack of growth in parenchymal innervation in cPrdm16KO relative to control samples (Figure 3E–I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is based on imaging and qPCR data (Figure 3E–I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–H).

claim: Sympathetic axon growth during early iWAT morphogenesis may be regulated by PRDM16-dependent signals.
source: These results indicate that early postnatal beige adipocytes indeed depend on PRDM16, the well-characterized transcriptional determinant of brown and beige adipocytes. Importantly, these data strongly suggest that sympathetic axon growth during early iWAT morphogenesis may be regulated by PRDM16-dependent signals.
evidence: This is inferred from the cPrdm16KO data showing loss of both beige adipocytes and sympathetic innervation.

claim: Prdm16 appears to be minimally expressed in white adipocytes in iWAT.
source: Altogether, Prdm16 appears to be minimally expressed in white adipocytes in iWAT, and thus its deletion in white adipocytes is likely to contribute minimally to the changes in sympathetic innervation.
evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data showing low Prdm16 expression in the dorsolateral region.

claim: Deletion of Prdm16 in iBAT does not affect its development or thermogenic function in young adults.
source: Interestingly, although PRDM16 also plays a critical role in brown adipocyte determination and function, deletion of Prdm16 in interscapular brown fat (iBAT) does not affect its development or thermogenic function in young adults (Cohen et al., 2014; Harms et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from Cohen et al., 2014; Harms et al., 2014.

claim: The role of PRDM16 in iBAT formation and function is compensated for by PRDM3.
source: Previous studies have shown that the role of PRDM16 in iBAT formation and function is compensated for by PRDM3, a transcriptional regulator closely related to PRDM16 (Harms et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from Harms et al., 2014.

claim: Similarly extensive sympathetic parenchymal innervation was detected in iBAT of both control and cPrdm16KO mice.
source: Consistent with these findings, we detected similarly extensive sympathetic parenchymal innervation in iBAT of both control and cPrdm16KO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2K–L).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 3—figure supplement 2K–L).

claim: Perinatal doxycycline treatment led to a strong reduction in Prdm16 in adipose depots at the mRNA level (70% reduction in the inguinal region of iWAT, 65% reduction in iBAT).
source: We first confirmed that perinatal doxycycline treatment led to a strong reduction in Prdm16 in adipose depots at the mRNA (70% reduction in the inguinal region of iWAT, 65% reduction in iBAT) and protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B).

claim: iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 5 weeks) and littermate control mice developed similarly with no difference in body mass.
source: Both iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 5 weeks) and littermate control mice developed similarly, with no difference in body mass (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on body weight measurements (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).

claim: Control inguinal regions exhibited robust increases in thermogenic markers following 2 days of cold exposure (e.g. 35-fold induction in Ucp1).
source: As expected, the control inguinal regions exhibited robust increases in the entire panel of thermogenic markers following 2 days of cold exposure (e.g. 35-fold induction in Ucp1) (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).

claim: Cold-induced increases in thermogenic markers were almost completely blocked following perinatal deletion of Prdm16.
source: In contrast, the cold-induced increases were almost completely blocked following perinatal deletion of Prdm16 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), mirroring our previous findings in constitutive Prdm16KO mice (Cohen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D) and cited from Cohen et al., 2014.

claim: Transient Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter adipocyte differentiation or function, as shown by Pparg, Fabp4, and Adipoq mRNA levels.
source: On the other hand, the transient Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter adipocyte differentiation or function, as shown by Pparg, Fabp4, and Adipoq mRNA levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).

claim: Gross features of sympathetic innervation such as nerve fascicles and blood vessel innervation were preserved in perinatal iPrdm16KO.
source: While the gross features of sympathetic innervation such as nerve fascicles and blood vessel innervation were preserved in perinatal iPrdm16KO, the parenchymal innervation that localized to the inguinal region of control iWAT was dramatically reduced in perinatal iPrdm16KO (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).

claim: Parenchymal innervation in the inguinal region of control iWAT was dramatically reduced in perinatal iPrdm16KO.
source: While the gross features of sympathetic innervation such as nerve fascicles and blood vessel innervation were preserved in perinatal iPrdm16KO, the parenchymal innervation that localized to the inguinal region of control iWAT was dramatically reduced in perinatal iPrdm16KO (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).

claim: Perinatal iPrdm16KO samples showed a 74.5% reduction in parenchymal neurite density compared to control samples when normalized to volume.
source: When neurite lengths were normalized to volumes of the isolated cuboids, perinatal iPrdm16KO samples showed a 74.5% reduction in parenchymal neurite density compared to control samples (Figure 4J, Figure 4—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 4J, Figure 4—figure supplement 2F).

claim: Perinatal iPrdm16KO showed a significant 52.8% decrease in neurite density when normalized by adipocyte density.
source: To rule out this possibility, we also calculated neurite density by factoring in adipocyte density from each tissue volume, and still observed a significant 52.8% decrease in density following perinatal Prdm16 deletion (Figure 4K, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 4K, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E–F).

claim: Perinatal Prdm16 knockout in adipocytes did not significantly affect thermogenic or adipogenic markers in iBAT.
source: Similar to our previous findings with the cPrdm16KO model, perinatal Prdm16 knockout in adipocytes did not significantly affect thermogenic or adipogenic markers in iBAT (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–B).

claim: Sympathetic parenchymal innervation levels did not appear different between control and perinatal iPrdm16KO iBAT samples.
source: In line with this, the sympathetic parenchymal innervation levels did not appear different between control and perinatal iPrdm16KO iBAT samples (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C–D).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C–D).

claim: TH+ fibers appeared substantially sparser in iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 8 weeks) than control.
source: Importantly, TH+ fibers still appeared substantially sparser in iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 8 weeks) than control (Figure 4—figure supplement 4E–J).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4—figure supplement 4E–J).

claim: Interactions between beige adipocytes and sympathetic nerve endings during an early critical developmental window are required for establishment of the sympathetic network in iWAT.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that interactions between beige adipocytes and sympathetic nerve endings during an early critical developmental window are required for establishment of the sympathetic network in iWAT, as perturbations during this window lead to lasting effects on parenchymal innervation density.
evidence: This is inferred from the perinatal Prdm16 deletion experiments showing lasting effects on innervation.

claim: Doxycycline treatment in adult mice led to a robust reduction in Prdm16 at the mRNA level (83% in the inguinal region of iWAT at RT).
source: As expected, doxycycline treatment in adult mice led to a robust reduction in Prdm16 at the mRNA (83% in the inguinal region of iWAT at RT) and protein levels (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).

claim: No body mass difference was observed between iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control mice.
source: No body mass difference was observed between iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on body weight measurements (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Significant attenuation of cold-induced upregulation in all thermogenic markers was observed following adult Prdm16 deletion.
source: We also observed significant attenuation of cold-induced upregulation in all thermogenic markers following Prdm16 deletion (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).

claim: Adult Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter markers of adipocyte differentiation.
source: Consistent with our previous findings, Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter markers of adipocyte differentiation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).

claim: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation was present in the inguinal regions of iWAT from both iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control samples.
source: Interestingly, we found dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation present in the inguinal regions of iWAT from both iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control samples (Figure 5C–H, Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 5C–H, Figure 4—video 1).

claim: Quantitative analysis resulted in a small, insignificant decrease (17.6%) in neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO relative to control samples when normalized by volume.
source: Quantitative analysis of the parenchymal neurite density (normalized by volume) from the 3D images resulted in a small, insignificant decrease (17.6%) in neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO relative to control samples (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 5I).

claim: Neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO was slightly higher (1.23-fold) than that of controls when normalized by adipocyte density.
source: Furthermore, as the adipocytes appeared larger in adult iPrdm16KO samples (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–J), we normalized neurite length by adipocyte density. As a result, we observed a reverse relationship with the neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO being slightly higher (1.23-fold) than that of controls (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 5J).

claim: Deleting Prdm16 in adipocytes of adult animals causes minimal changes in sympathetic parenchymal neurite density.
source: These results suggest that the small density difference when normalized by volume is likely driven by a scaling effect rather than actual neurite remodeling. Importantly, these data indicate that deleting Prdm16 in adipocytes of adult animals causes minimal changes in sympathetic parenchymal neurite density, strongly supporting the early postnatal period being the critical window during which interactions between beige adipocytes and sympathetic nerve endings occur.
evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative analysis showing no significant change in innervation after adult Prdm16 deletion.

claim: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation is observed in both iBAT and the inguinal region of iWAT where beige adipocytes are primarily located.
source: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation is observed in both iBAT and the inguinal region of iWAT, where beige adipocytes are primarily located; however, sparse innervation is found in eWAT and the dorsolateral region of iWAT, an area of the tissue that is devoid of beige adipocytes even under long term cold stimulation (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).

claim: Sparse innervation is found in eWAT and the dorsolateral region of iWAT, areas devoid of beige adipocytes even under long term cold stimulation.
source: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation is observed in both iBAT and the inguinal region of iWAT, where beige adipocytes are primarily located; however, sparse innervation is found in eWAT and the dorsolateral region of iWAT, an area of the tissue that is devoid of beige adipocytes even under long term cold stimulation (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).

claim: The appearance of UCP1+ beige adipocytes precedes the emergence of dense parenchymal neurites during early postnatal development.
source: Importantly, the appearance of UCP1+ beige adipocytes precedes the emergence of dense parenchymal neurites during early postnatal development.
evidence: This is based on the temporal analysis of UCP1+ adipocytes and TH+ neurites in the manuscript.

claim: Sympathetic fibers travel in nerve fascicles to arrive at iWAT, and then depart from nerve fascicles to reach main blood vessels within iWAT.
source: We observed that sympathetic fibers travel in nerve fascicles to arrive at iWAT, and then depart from nerve fascicles to reach main blood vessels within iWAT.
evidence: This is based on imaging observations described in the Results section.

claim: By P6, the sympathetic innervation on blood vessels demonstrated a dense mesh-like structure, resembling that of mature iWAT.
source: By P6, the sympathetic innervation on blood vessels demonstrated a dense mesh-like structure, resembling that of mature iWAT.
evidence: This is based on imaging observations described in the Results section.

claim: Vasculature serves as a guide to direct developing sympathetic fibers to reach their targets.
source: However, dense parenchymal innervation surrounding adipocytes, which several studies have characterized in mature iWAT (Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017), is not established at P6. Instead, we observed sparse discrete sympathetic fibers and small vessels in congruence within the tissue parenchyma, a common phenomenon in sympathetic nerve fiber development where vasculature serves as a guide to direct developing fibers to reach their targets, such as the heart (Nam et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Nam et al., 2013.

claim: Early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice born and raised at thermoneutrality with minimal sympathetic activity.
source: Although beige adipocyte recruitment in adult mice requires sympathetic stimulation, early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice born and raised at thermoneutrality with minimal sympathetic activity as well as in mice with genetic sympathetic ablation (Wu et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is based on the thermoneutrality data in the manuscript and cited from Wu et al., 2020b.

claim: Early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice with genetic sympathetic ablation.
source: Although beige adipocyte recruitment in adult mice requires sympathetic stimulation, early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice born and raised at thermoneutrality with minimal sympathetic activity as well as in mice with genetic sympathetic ablation (Wu et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is cited from Wu et al., 2020b.

claim: Adipocytes or their progenitors in different regions of iWAT may exhibit unique properties.
source: Interestingly, we found several genes involved in the transcriptional control of beige adipocyte determination and function to have higher expression levels in the inguinal than the dorsolumbar region throughout early development, suggesting adipocytes or their progenitors in different regions may exhibit unique properties.
evidence: This is inferred from the regional gene expression differences observed in the manuscript.

claim: The whole-tissue UCP1+ patterns at P21 and P28 closely resemble that of adult mice following cold exposure.
source: It is also worth noting that the whole-tissue UCP1+ patterns at P21 and P28 closely resemble that of adult mice following cold exposure.
evidence: This is based on comparison of imaging data from different ages and conditions.

claim: The thermogenic gene expression of early postnatal beige adipocytes diminishes as mice mature.
source: In addition, the thermogenic gene expression of early postnatal beige adipocytes diminishes as mice mature.
evidence: This is based on qPCR data showing peak expression at P14 followed by decline.

claim: Early postnatal beige adipocytes may express PRDM16-dependent neurotrophic factors that stimulate sympathetic axon growth or downregulate inhibition cues.
source: Our findings suggest that early postnatal beige adipocytes may express PRDM16-dependent neurotrophic factors that stimulate sympathetic axon growth or downregulate inhibition cues.
evidence: This is speculated based on the Prdm16 deletion experiments showing reduced innervation.

claim: S100b showed a regional pattern at the mRNA level during early iWAT development, with higher expression in the inguinal region in a PRDM16-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, S100b, but not Tgfb1, showed a regional pattern at the mRNA level during early iWAT development, with higher expression in the inguinal region in a PRDM16-dependent manner (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F).

claim: S100B may be one of the potential cues in regulating iWAT sympathetic development.
source: This result suggests that S100B may be one of the potential cues in regulating iWAT sympathetic development.
evidence: This is inferred from the regional and PRDM16-dependent expression pattern of S100b.

claim: Sympathetic neurites may be indirectly regulated by additional beige adipocyte-associated cell types, such as immune or stromal cells.
source: It is also likely that sympathetic neurites are indirectly regulated by additional beige adipocyte-associated cell types, such as immune or stromal cells.
evidence: This is speculated as a possible mechanism.

claim: Sympathetic neurites in iWAT respond to signals from beige adipocytes or associated cells during early development.
source: These results indicate that sympathetic neurites in iWAT respond to signals from beige adipocytes or associated cells during early development.
evidence: This is inferred from the perinatal Prdm16 deletion experiments.

claim: When the innervation pattern is fully established, signals from beige adipocytes are no longer required for maintaining the innervation level during adulthood.
source: However, when the innervation pattern is fully established, such signals are no longer required for maintaining the innervation level during adulthood.
evidence: This is inferred from the adult Prdm16 deletion experiments showing no effect on innervation.

claim: Cold-induced beige adipocytes do not promote sympathetic neurite outgrowth in adult iWAT when equivalent tissue regions are compared.
source: In line with this, we have previously shown that cold-induced beige adipocytes do not promote sympathetic neurite outgrowth in adult iWAT when equivalent tissue regions are compared.
evidence: This is cited from the authors' previous work.

claim: Sympathetic neurite density is regulated by local cues from beige adipocytes during a specific developmental window and exhibits limited plasticity once the pattern is established.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that sympathetic neurite density is regulated by local cues from beige adipocytes during a specific developmental window and exhibits limited plasticity once the pattern is established.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: Chronic leptin treatment acting on hypothalamic neurons was found to rescue the defect in sympathetic innervation in iBAT and iWAT of adult leptin-deficient mice.
source: Of note, a recent study demonstrated leptin-mediated central regulation of sympathetic innervation in adipose tissue (Wang et al., 2020). Specifically, chronic leptin treatment acting on hypothalamic neurons was found to rescue the defect in sympathetic innervation in iBAT and iWAT of adult leptin-deficient mice.
evidence: This is cited from Wang et al., 2020.

claim: The sympathetic axon growth period observed (P10-P21) largely overlaps with a postnatal leptin surge (P8-P20) reported previously.
source: Interestingly, the sympathetic axon growth period we observed (P10-P21) largely overlaps with a postnatal leptin surge (P8-P20) reported previously (Ahima et al., 1998; Wu et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is based on comparison with cited literature (Ahima et al., 1998; Wu et al., 2020a).

claim: Thermogenic adipocytes have been demonstrated to provide metabolic benefits that may combat obesity and associated metabolic diseases.
source: Thermogenic adipocytes have been demonstrated to provide metabolic benefits that may combat obesity and associated metabolic diseases.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge in the field.
